nodes.summary: Configures TypeScript checking for HTTP recorder tests and source with bundler resolution and no emitted output.

nodes.summary: Provides ambient TypeScript declarations for SST-generated environment bindings used by the HTTP API code generator package.

nodes.name: pack
nodes.summary: Builds the HTTP recorder package, rewrites package exports for distribution, and creates its npm archive.

nodes.name: withPackedArchive
nodes.summary: Runs a callback with a newly packed HTTP recorder archive and deletes that archive when the callback finishes.

nodes.name: verifyPackage
nodes.summary: Installs the packed archive into an isolated consumer and verifies its public exports, TypeScript declarations, and blocked deep imports.

nodes.name: compile
nodes.summary: Validates HTTP API groups and endpoint schemas, then normalizes them into the internal contract used by generators.

nodes.name: emitEffect

nodes.name: emitEffectImported
nodes.summary: Generates Effect API files that reuse endpoint and schema exports supplied by existing modules.

nodes.name: emitEffectShape

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent, and the README lists the installation routes and the desktop app. CONTRIBUTING.md covers the development setup, package structure, and verification expectations used throughout the repository. Read these two documents first to learn the vocabulary the rest of this tour relies on.

tour.title: Monorepo Layout
tour.description: The root package.json defines a private Bun monorepo with workspace packages and shared dependency catalogs, so all packages are built and versioned together. turbo.json tells Turborepo which tasks depend on each other, which outputs to cache, and how tests behave. tsconfig.json extends a shared Bun TypeScript configuration, so each package inherits the same compiler settings.

tour.title: Shared Contracts
tour.description: The schema package holds the Effect Schema definitions that describe data shared across packages, including the configuration format in config.ts. Building on the monorepo layout, these definitions are the typed contract that other layers validate against. Learn these shapes early because the runtime, API, and UI all refer back to them.
tour.languageLesson: Effect Schema lets one declaration produce both a TypeScript type and a runtime decoder, so data is checked at the boundary instead of trusted.

tour.title: Core Runtime Foundations
tour.description: The core package holds the agent runtime. bus.ts is among the most imported files in the graph (about 66 importers), and location.ts has about 54, so these modules are the shared plumbing for the rest of core. instance.ts manages the running instance that these modules operate within.

tour.title: Plugin System
tour.description: Building on the core runtime, the plugin directory holds the extension wiring. internal.ts has the highest outgoing dependency count in the graph (about 93), which makes it a good map of how built-in capabilities connect. provider.ts sits beside it as the companion module in the same folder.

tour.title: AI Model Layer
tour.description: llm.ts is the top-level LLM API, exposing generate, stream, request, and structured generateObject calls with response parsing. It depends on the route client module below it, which handles the lower-level request path. The schema index is the most widely imported file in the graph (about 144 importers), so its types form the vocabulary of the AI layer.

tour.title: Persistence and Migrations
tour.description: The data layer uses Drizzle over SQLite, and core keeps a migration module in its database folder to manage schema changes. The artifact table from the update service shows a migration in practice: it is keyed by channel, name, distribution, and version, and it stores activation metadata. Migration files are numbered, so the schema evolves in a fixed order alongside the code.
tour.languageLesson: Migrations should be append-only: a new numbered file changes the schema instead of editing an old one, so every environment can replay the same history.

tour.title: API Contract and Client
tour.description: The client package is the typed bridge between the runtime and its callers. contract.ts defines the API contract, and effect/client.ts builds an Effect-based client on top of it. Callers depend on this contract rather than on server internals, which is why the API layer is documented as a separate step.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The CLI package provides the command-line surface for OpenCode, and its source index is the module that exposes that functionality. The CLI Dockerfile packages it into a container image built from prebuilt musl binaries for the selected architecture. Packaging for a target platform lives in its own file, separate from the application code.
tour.languageLesson: In Dockerfiles, layer order drives build caching: put rarely changing steps such as OS packages before frequently changing application code.

tour.title: Terminal User Interface
tour.description: The TUI package renders the terminal interface, and app.tsx is its root component. It has about 70 outgoing dependencies, so reading it gives a map of the whole screen. theme.tsx supplies shared styling through a context provider that the components below it consume.
tour.languageLesson: Context providers supply shared values such as the theme to deeply nested components without passing props through every level.

tour.title: Web App and Server Registry
tour.description: The web app root composes query, typography, and base provider wrappers around the interface. The server registry helpers normalize server URLs, group servers with their projects, and handle removal checks, so the app knows which runtime servers it can reach. Both the web and desktop surfaces belong to the client-facing layer.

tour.title: CI/CD and Container Builds
tour.description: test.yml runs affected-package analysis, unit tests, and end-to-end tests on pushes and pull requests, so changes are verified against the packages they touch. publish.yml prepares versions and builds platform-specific CLI and app artifacts for release. The stats server Dockerfile shows a multi-stage build that prunes the monorepo before installing filtered dependencies.
tour.languageLesson: In GitHub Actions, on sets the triggers, jobs run in parallel by default, and steps run in order within a single job.

tour.title: Tooling and Lint Rules
tour.description: The repository ships custom oxlint rules under script/oxlint/anti-slop, with each rule in its own module under rules/. The .oxlintrc.json configuration controls which rules apply across the codebase. Reading the rule set shows the code-quality conventions that changes are checked against.
tour.languageLesson: Custom lint rules are usually AST visitors that flag specific syntax patterns, so the check runs automatically on every change.
